title: Robert W. Taylor
name: Robert W. Taylor
summary: American computer-science research leader whose work at ARPA, Xerox PARC, and DEC supported major advances in networking and personal computing.
whyThisMatters: Taylor's influence was organizational as well as technical: he assembled and funded research groups that produced foundational networked-computing systems. This is relevant to hacker and security history because it situates later network practice in its institutional and technical origins.

sections.overview:
Robert William Taylor was an American computer-science research manager and leader. He worked at ARPA during the formative period of interactive-computing and networking research.

Networks and personal computing

The Computer History Museum credits Taylor with initiating ARPANET and with sponsoring interactive-computing research. At Xerox PARC, he founded the Computer Science Laboratory, where teams worked on Ethernet, the Alto, and networked personal-computing systems.

In memoriam

Taylor retired in 1996 and died in 2017. His record is a reminder that major computing systems are built by communities of engineers and researchers, with program leadership helping sustain their work.

timeline.event: Becomes director of ARPA's Information Processing Techniques Office.
Leaves ARPA after the initial ARPANET program period.
Founds the Computer Science Laboratory at Xerox PARC.
Becomes founding director of DEC's Systems Research Center.
